---
title: "Indicator family: Health survey indicators, British Columbia"
---

*Status: a published indicator family (milestone M3 in progress). Regenerate
all series with `uv run sohbc build`.*

This page covers the family of British Columbia indicators that the
pipeline extracts from a single Statistics Canada survey table, widening
the project beyond mortality into physical morbidity, mental health,
subjective wellbeing, social wellbeing, and access to care. Each series is
published as its own versioned tidy dataset and trend files; the [life
satisfaction](indicator-life-satisfaction-bc.qmd) series has its own
worked page.

## Provenance

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Domains** | [Physical morbidity, mental health, subjective wellbeing, social wellbeing](../reference/measurement-framework.qmd) |
| **Definition** | Share of British Columbians aged 18 and over reporting each measured characteristic, annual 2015–2025 [@statcan_health_indicators] |
| **Source** | Statistics Canada, table 13-10-0905-01, *Health indicator statistics, annual estimates* (Canadian Community Health Survey) [@statcan_health_indicators] |
| **Access** | Statistics Canada Web Data Service (automated full-table download) |
| **Form** | indicator table (published survey summary statistics) |
| **Geography** | British Columbia (this table has no sub-provincial rows; the [regional view](#the-regional-view) uses table 13-10-0972-01) |
| **Coverage** | 2015–2025 (annual); observation window shown on each figure |
| **Frequency / refresh** | annual |
| **Licence** | Statistics Canada Open Licence |
| **Proxy note** | Self-reported proxies, not the state of health itself ([why](../explanation/definition-of-health.qmd#proxies-are-not-the-state-of-health)) |

## The family

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
tLife = await FileAttachment("../data/published/life_satisfaction_bc_trend.json").json()
tPhyH = await FileAttachment("../data/published/perceived_health_fair_poor_bc_trend.json").json()
tMentH = await FileAttachment("../data/published/perceived_mental_health_fair_poor_bc_trend.json").json()
tBelong = await FileAttachment("../data/published/sense_of_belonging_bc_trend.json").json()
tAnx = await FileAttachment("../data/published/anxiety_disorder_bc_trend.json").json()
tMood = await FileAttachment("../data/published/mood_disorder_bc_trend.json").json()
tDiab = await FileAttachment("../data/published/diabetes_bc_trend.json").json()
tBp = await FileAttachment("../data/published/high_blood_pressure_bc_trend.json").json()
tProv = await FileAttachment("../data/published/has_regular_provider_bc_trend.json").json()
tSmoke = await FileAttachment("../data/published/smoker_daily_bc_trend.json").json()
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
series = [
  {key: "life_satisfaction_bc", label: "Life satisfaction", domain: "Subjective wellbeing", direction: "higher is better", trend: tLife},
  {key: "perceived_health_fair_poor_bc", label: "Perceived health, fair or poor", domain: "Subjective wellbeing", direction: "lower is better", trend: tPhyH},
  {key: "perceived_mental_health_fair_poor_bc", label: "Perceived mental health, fair or poor", domain: "Mental health", direction: "lower is better", trend: tMentH},
  {key: "sense_of_belonging_bc", label: "Sense of belonging to local community", domain: "Social wellbeing", direction: "higher is better", trend: tBelong},
  {key: "anxiety_disorder_bc", label: "Anxiety disorder", domain: "Mental health", direction: "lower is better", trend: tAnx},
  {key: "mood_disorder_bc", label: "Mood disorder", domain: "Mental health", direction: "lower is better", trend: tMood},
  {key: "diabetes_bc", label: "Diabetes", domain: "Physical morbidity", direction: "lower is better", trend: tDiab},
  {key: "high_blood_pressure_bc", label: "High blood pressure", domain: "Physical morbidity", direction: "lower is better", trend: tBp},
  {key: "has_regular_provider_bc", label: "Has a regular healthcare provider", domain: "Access to care", direction: "higher is better", trend: tProv},
  {key: "smoker_daily_bc", label: "Current daily smoker", domain: "Physical morbidity", direction: "lower is better", trend: tSmoke}
]
family = series.map(s => {
  const t = s.trend
  const segs = t.segments.length > 1
    ? t.segments.map(g => `${g.slope_per_decade.toFixed(1)} (${g.start}–${g.end})`).join("; ")
    : "single regime"
  return {
    label: s.label,
    domain: s.domain,
    direction: s.direction,
    slope_per_decade: t.overall.slope_per_decade,
    verdict: t.stationarity.verdict,
    change_point: t.change_point ?? "—",
    segments: segs
  }
})
Inputs.table(family, {
  columns: ["label", "domain", "direction", "slope_per_decade", "verdict", "change_point", "segments"],
  header: {
    label: "series", domain: "domain", direction: "better if…",
    slope_per_decade: "slope/decade (pp)", verdict: "stationarity",
    change_point: "largest break", segments: "regimes (pp/decade)"
  },
  width: {label: 210, segments: 240}
})
```

Each slope is in percentage points per decade over 2015–2025, for both
sexes; a positive slope is not automatically good or bad — the *better
if…* column states the direction that the measurement treats as
favourable. `stationarity` is the pipeline's label from the formal tests
(stationary, nonstationary, or undetermined where the series is too short
for the test to have power); `largest break` is the BIC-selected change
point, where one exists.

## What the family shows

The series are not all moving the same way, and the direction of movement
follows the direction of the measurement:

- **Wellbeing is falling.** Life satisfaction (`-11.4` pp/decade;
  break at 2021) and sense of belonging (`-10.9` pp/decade; break at
  2021) both fell sharply.
- **Poor self-rated state is rising.** Perceived mental health fair or
  poor rose `+12.7` pp/decade and perceived health fair or poor `+4.3`
  pp/decade; both are nonstationary (perceived health has no dated break).
- **Mental-health conditions are rising.** Anxiety (`+6.2` pp/decade) and
  mood disorders (`+3.0` pp/decade) both increased; neither carries a
  dated break in the current build.
- **Some behaviours improve.** Daily smoking fell `-4.4` pp/decade, though
  the regime split at 2021 shows the decline flattening after 2021
  (`-7.8` before, `-4.4` after).
- **Three series are flat.** Diabetes (`+0.9`), high blood pressure
  (`+2.6`), and having a regular healthcare provider (`-2.1`) are labelled
  **stationary** over their short windows — no evidence of a trend beyond
  year-to-year noise.

Read together, the family is a picture of rising self-reported distress
and falling life evaluation over a decade, with the clearest breaks
coinciding with 2020. The pipeline dates those breaks; this page does not
claim they are caused by the pandemic.

## The regional view

The same nine measures (all but *has a regular healthcare provider*,
which the table does not carry) are published for BC's 16 health service
delivery areas from Statistics Canada table 13-10-0972-01
[@statcan_health_regions_cchs], as five pooled two-year periods over the
same 2015–2024 window.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
reg = await FileAttachment("../data/published/cchs_bc_regions_summary.json").json()
shortRegion = n => n.replace(" Health Service Delivery Area", "")
regRows = reg.series.map(s => {
  const spread = s.spread.health_service_delivery_area
  const period = reg.reference_periods[reg.reference_periods.length - 1]
  const key = spread[period] ? period : Object.keys(spread).sort().pop()
  const d = spread[key]
  return {
    indicator: s.indicator.replace(", satisfied or very satisfied", "").replace(", somewhat strong or very strong", "").replace(", fair or poor", " (fair/poor)"),
    period: key,
    lowest: `${d.lowest.value.toFixed(1)} (${shortRegion(d.lowest.region)})`,
    highest: `${d.highest.value.toFixed(1)} (${shortRegion(d.highest.region)})`,
    ratio: d.ratio,
    range: d.range
  }
})
Inputs.table(regRows, {
  columns: ["indicator", "period", "lowest", "highest", "ratio", "range"],
  header: {indicator: "series", period: "period", lowest: "lowest area", highest: "highest area", ratio: "ratio", range: "range (pp)"},
  width: {indicator: 190, lowest: 170, highest: 170}
})
```

The regional gap is wide and it does not simply mirror the provincial
level: daily smoking varies about **3×** across areas, diabetes **2.5×**,
and mood disorder **2.2×**, while life satisfaction — the flattest
regional distribution — still spans 9 percentage points. Areas do not
rank the same way on every series: Vancouver-metro areas sit lowest on
smoking and diabetes but also lowest on sense of belonging.

Each area's slope over the five pooled periods is published in the
summary file, but with five points the stationarity verdict is
**undetermined** for every regional series — the trend test has no power
here, and the regional view reports levels and gaps, not dated regimes.
Anxiety disorder is absent from the 2023/2024 period entirely, so its
regional spread stops at 2021/2022. Cells flagged *too unreliable to
publish* are kept in the tidy file with their status and excluded from
the summaries.

## Caveats

- **Survey estimate.** Every series is self-reported on a national survey,
  carrying sampling error and a coefficient-of-variation release policy;
  some cells are suppressed or flagged. Plotted values are published point
  estimates.
- **Measurement, not only change.** The CCHS collection frame changed over
  the series and 2020–2021 collection was disrupted by the pandemic [@statcan_health_indicators].
  A step in a series may be a step in the measurement. Direction of the
  breaks is dated, not attributed.
- **Short window.** Ten annual points is a short series; the
  stationarity test has limited power, which is why some series are
  labelled *undetermined* rather than stationary.
- **Self-report and definition drift.** "Percent" mixes reported
  behaviour, diagnosed conditions, and self-rated state; each has a
  different relationship to health, and a survey question that changes
  wording does not change meaninglessly.
- **Provincial table, separate regional product.** Table 13-10-0905-01
  is provincial only. The [regional view](#the-regional-view) comes from
  a different table (13-10-0972-01) of pooled two-year periods with
  narrower indicator coverage and heavier suppression — a distinct
  product, not a disaggregation of the annual series.
- **Revisions.** Statistics Canada may revise estimates; the published
  files are regenerated from the source on each build.

## Reproduce

```bash
uv run sohbc fetch statcan_health_indicators statcan_health_regions_cchs
uv run sohbc build
```

Every series publishes `data/published/<key>.csv`,
`data/published/<key>_trend.json`, and
`data/published/<key>_by_sex_trend.json`. The regional view publishes
`data/published/cchs_bc_regions.csv` and
`data/published/cchs_bc_regions_summary.json`. The selection and
definitions are in `src/sohbc/indicators.py`; add or remove a series
there and rebuild.
